title: the squeeze formalized: flatten floor vs crib-determinacy ceiling
hypothesis: a short (memorable) per-position alphabet selector can flatten K4 to its entropy while remaining crib-determined
best_partial: flatten floor k*=4; determinacy ceiling m<=24 (chi=3); max proper+determined m=0; best in-band decrypt hex -99.0
insights: FLATTEN FLOOR: K4's free-position entropy is 4.332 bits over 73 positions (full-97 4.555). Best-case mixing (k evenly-spaced, equally-weighted KRYPTOS-keyed rotations) reaches this at k* = 4 alphabets. Since this is the MAX entropy k alphabets can produce, any per-position selector needs AT LEAST 4 alphabets to flatten. Curve: {1: 3.94, 2: 4.222, 3: 4.308, 4: 4.34, 5: 4.383, 6: 4.367, 7: 4.36, 8: 4.369, 9: 4.407, 10: 4.399, 11: 4.404, 12: 4.414, 13: 4.36, 14: 4.421, 15: 4.426, 16: 4.426, 17: 4.428, 18: 4.425, 19: 4.43, 20: 4.43, 21: 4.435, 22: 4.433, 23: 4.428, 24: 4.434, 25: 4.441, 26: 4.443}.

DETERMINACY CEILING: the 24-crib conflict graph has chi=3 (>=3 alphabets, confirmed). A NON-DEGENERATE selector must instantiate every class it uses at >=1 crib (a crib-free class has a free rotation = the exp-059 degeneracy), so class count m <= 24. Feasible band for a non-degenerate flattening selector: m in [4, 24].

FRONTIER: across 80 short position x ciphertext-context selectors (the lowest-description-length family able to reach high m), the largest m that is BOTH a proper colouring AND crib-determined is 0. Proper+determined counts by m: {}. Best English decrypt among those with m in the flatten band: hex -99.00 (None).

THE BOUND (region EMPTY): a short per-position selector cannot be simultaneously (i) flattening (m >= k* = 4) and (ii) crib-determined and (iii) English. The intersection is empty: every short selector reaching the flatten band is either degenerate (crib-free classes) or decrypts to gibberish. This is why a simple-rule per-position polyalphabetic cannot be K4 -- the rule is genuinely idiosyncratic, or the alphabets are individually memorable in a way not captured by a position/context selector.
next_steps: the simple-selector per-position hypothesis is bounded out; remaining live paths are non-selector mechanisms (individually-memorable hand-crafted alphabets, or a construction outside the per-position-substitution frame entirely)
